correctness.rationale: The primary source independently proves the lower bound: no n-chain from L reaches B_n, even with merely nonempty intersections. For the upper bound, a positive legal cylinder beginning ab lies in L and in a^2L because applying a^{-2} changes its initial pair to a^{-1}b, also a positive transition in the source matrix. The nonsingularized action preserves positivity under translation, so every consecutive pair a^{2j}L and a^{2j+2}L has positive overlap. Finally a positive legal cylinder beginning b, translated by a^{2n+2}, lies in both a^{2n+2}L and B_n. Thus an (n+1)-chain exists and the lower bound is sharp.
